title: Add engineering guardrails to BeastMaster skills
description:
## Summary
Add firm maintainability and production-readiness guardrails to CreatureCreator agent workflows.

## User Mandate
> `>-` needs to be `|` in the skills, which I fixed in the agent file already (it wasn't being discovered). I want firm code guidelines involved too like in some of the others. There are agent tasks in one of the repos (ICW I think) about recurring problems like code duplication and reinvention, unclear/unconsolidated ownership, overwrought pre-engineering, etc. I want this repo to be more slimmed down as well, since these are classic pitfalls of agentic development. I had an external agent provide this guidance on common agentic software development pitfalls in order to ensure our repo's agents are fully capable of avoiding them

STRICT. Use literal-block descriptions in skills. Add firm guidance against duplication, type evasion, comprehension debt, premature architecture, unclear ownership, and incomplete production behavior. Keep the base agent slim through graduated discovery.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Implemented the requested guardrails inside CreatureCreator only. Added `.github/skills/engineering-guardrails/SKILL.md` with firm rules for type integrity, no blind casts or null-forgiving shortcuts, single-source ownership, duplication and tracker deduplication, intent-before-implementation, bounded scope, and production-readiness checks for invalid input, cancellation, retry, disposal, determinism, stale results, and meaningful observability. Updated `creature-workflow` to use `description: |` and load the guardrails for code, refactor, and architecture work. Updated BeastMaster graduated discovery to include the skill. Focused validation passed after removing one trailing whitespace defect: all frontmatter is valid, all relative links resolve, no `>-` remains, and `git diff --check` passes. ICW evidence used: canonical task ownership and deduplication in `docs/tasks/active-tasks.md`, explicit speculative-recommendation limits in the ICW council skill, and idempotent cleanup/ownership guidance in ICW handoffs.
